A noble griffon — the fierce hooked-beak head and golden feathered wings of a giant eagle fused to the powerful tawny body, haunches and lashing tail of a lion, talons gripping the rock, amber eyes blazing with sovereign fury.

A colossal kraken heaving from the deep — a mountainous mottled-purple body and vast barnacled tentacles, each thicker than a ship's mast, lined with pale suckers, a single baleful eye the size of a wagon wheel burning cold yellow.

A blazing phoenix of living fire — a great hawk-like bird wreathed in gold-and-crimson flame, feathers trailing live embers, wings of pure fire spread wide, eyes like white-hot coals, every wingbeat sending cascades of molten sparks into the dark.

A many-headed hydra rising from black water — a serpentine body scaled in overlapping olive-green armor, nine long necks each crowned with a slavering fanged head, each neck weaving independently, acid-yellow eyes and forked tongues tasting the air in unison.

A towering treant of living oak — a vast humanoid form of gnarled bark and heartwood, mossy shoulders broad as barn walls, roots trailing like feet, branch-fingers crackling with new leaves, amber sap weeping from ancient wound-scars, one hollow eye aglow with green foxfire.

A monstrous troll — a hunched boulder-shouldered brute of grey-green warty hide thick as rhinoceros leather, long knuckle-dragging arms, a flat squashed nose, broken tusk-teeth jutting from a wet gaping jaw, stringy hair matted with mud, regenerating flesh visibly knitting over fresh wounds.

A basilisk — a massive eight-legged reptile of dull iron-green scales, crested skull low and heavy, walking with a slow deliberate swagger, its signature feature two enormous pale-gold eyes radiating faint crystalline light that turns living flesh to cold grey stone.

A chimera — a grotesque triple-natured beast: the great maned lion's head and muscular forebody fused to a goat's horned head erupting from the spine midway, the hindquarters tapering into a living serpent neck and fanged head for a tail, scales and fur colliding.

A hulking minotaur — a massively muscled human body standing eight feet tall, covered in short dark-brown fur at the shoulders and arms, crowned with the broad horned head of a bull, black hooves, nostrils flaring red, a double-headed axe gripped in enormous fists.

A mountain giant — a fifty-foot humanoid of granite-grey skin rough as quarry stone, clad in pelts of whole bears, a craggy boulder-like face half-buried in a tangled iron beard, each footfall cracking the earth, one hand closing around an uprooted pine for a club.

A sphinx — a regal creature with a calm human face of burnished gold skin and kohl-dark eyes, a muscular lion's body of tawny fur, and broad feathered wings folded with geometric precision, seated on worn sandstone, radiating patient immortal intelligence from its unblinking gaze.

A manticore — the tawny lion body rippling with muscle, a disturbingly human face split by rows upon rows of shark-like teeth, a long scorpion tail arched high and bristling with iron-hard venomous spines it can launch like darts, red mane wild in the wind.

A cyclops — a cave-dwelling titan of pale scarred skin, fifteen feet of knotted muscle, one enormous brown eye dominating a broad flat face above a wide mouth of uneven teeth, a roughly-hewn club across its shoulder, sheep-hide draped over one arm.

A cerberus — three wolf-like heads on thick-muscled necks rising from one massive hound body of coal-black fur, each head snarling independently to reveal bone-white fangs, a serpent for a tail rearing and hissing, ember-red eyes in each face smoldering with underworld heat.

A colossal sea-serpent leviathan — a sinuous body three hundred feet of blue-black scale, a horse-like finned head trailing bioluminescent whiskers, crest of membranous spines running the full length, water sheeting from armored flanks as it breaches, one ancient amber eye clearing the surface.

A winged pegasus — a powerful white stallion of shining satin coat and perfectly sculpted muscle, from whose withers spring two enormous feathered wings of pure white primary feathers edged in silver, the great pinions unfurling with a sound like sails catching a full gale.

A frost giant — a twenty-foot figure of pale blue-white skin webbed with frost-crack patterns, long white hair rimed with ice, clad in mammoth hide and iron, exhaling visible clouds of killing cold, one massive fist encasing a glacier-blue club of carved ancient ice.

A kelpie — at first glance a sleek grey horse standing at a river's edge, coat glistening wet, mane flowing like dark water, but hooves reversed, eyes pale and pupilless as river stone, its signature horror a hide that bonds to any rider's hand on contact.

A great owlbear — a hulking beast of bear mass and proportion covered in tawny-brown feathers grading to dark barred plumage at the shoulders, a wide flat owl's face of bone-pale facial disc, hooked beak, and enormous amber eyes, great curved bear-claws raking the forest floor.

A wendigo — a gaunt towering horror of exposed grey skin and jutting bone, antlered skull for a head with hollow black eye sockets lit by cold blue hunger-light, emaciated limbs impossibly long, breath a plume of killing frost, surrounded by the sound of howling winter wind.

A stone gargoyle come alive — a roughly man-sized figure of animated grey limestone, bat-like wings of solid rock spreading with a grinding crack, a grotesque horned face of chiseled snarl, taloned hands flexing, fissures in its stone skin glowing red-orange from the heat of sudden life within.

A hippogriff — eagle head and fearsome talons, a chest of brown-barred flight feathers tapering to the sleek muscled hindquarters and hooves of a horse, wings of vast span half-raised for balance, built leaner and swifter than a griffon, fierce golden eyes locked on the horizon.

A roc — an eagle of continental scale, each wing spanning a full mile of shadow, feathers like bronze shields, a head the size of a house with a hooked beak capable of seizing an elephant whole, the wind from a single wingbeat flattening forests below.

A cockatrice — a grotesque chimera the size of a large rooster, reptilian scaled body and bat-leather wings, the head of a crowing cock with wattled comb, a serpent tail barbed at its tip, its signature feature a golden stare that transforms warm flesh to cold stone.

A banshee wraith — a tall translucent female figure of pale ghostlight, robes of shredded silver mist billowing without wind, long hair streaming upward, hollow eyes pouring white luminescence, her mouth open in the one devastating feature — a shriek of pure grief that stops a living heart.

A many-headed hydra rising from the swamp — a serpentine body thick as a fallen oak, scales of dark olive-green slicked with marsh slime, nine long necks each crowned with a fanged horned head, each severed neck sprouting two replacements instantly.

A stone gargoyle alive — a creature of carved granite given terrible motion, bat-like wings of solid stone spreading with a grinding shriek, a grotesque horned face with a wide fanged maw, clawed hands of chiseled rock, eyes suddenly flooding with burning amber light in the dark.

A banshee — a spectral female form trailing ragged shrouds of pale mist, her body half-translucent revealing the faint outline of bone, hollow eyes blazing with cold white light, long hair streaming like smoke in a wind no one else feels, her open mouth releasing a wail that stops hearts.

A many-headed hydra — a vast serpentine body of dark green scaled hide rising from the swamp, nine long necks weaving independently, each crowned with a wedge-shaped fanged head dripping venom, every severed stump sprouting two new necks already writhing.

A giant of the mountains — a man-shaped colossus forty feet tall, skin like weathered granite, a beard of tangled grey rock-dust, hands that can cup a boulder easily, eyes pale as glacier ice, each footfall cracking the ridge beneath immense stony weight.

A colossal sea-serpent — a leviathan of dark emerald-green scales half a mile in length, a neck thick as a warship rising from the ocean, a flat spade-shaped head bearing rows of backward-curving teeth, a great dorsal crest of translucent fin catching the light like stained glass.

A many-headed hydra rising from black swamp water — nine serpentine necks erupting from a single scaled torso of oily green-black, each wedge-shaped head bearing rows of recurved fangs, forked tongues tasting the air, the central neck thicker than an oak trunk.

A basilisk crouching on shattered stone — a massive eight-legged reptile with armored olive-brown scales, a low crested skull, and two enormous forward-facing eyes of molten gold-green that radiate a visible distortion, its signature petrifying gaze capable of turning flesh to cold grey rock.

Cerberus — three massive mastiff heads on a single body of night-black muscle the size of a draft horse, each neck thick as a barrel with a mane of writhing serpents, six amber eyes glowing ember-red, a serpent's tail coiled and hissing, guarding a gate of black iron.

A colossal sea-serpent breaching the swells — a hundred feet of armored neck and neck rising from thrashing white water, scales of deep teal and gunmetal interlocked like shields, a horse-like skull bearing long recurved fangs, the vast coiling body generating a whirlpool as it turns.

A kelpie emerging from dark water — a sleek horse of impossible deep-black coat gleaming with a permanent wet sheen, mane trailing like river weed, eyes a luminous pale green, hooves silent on soft ground, the body radiating cold river-damp, a creature of drowning patience and terrible beauty.

A basilisk crouching low in the ruins — a massive eight-legged reptile of dark chitinous scales, heavy crested skull, thick serpentine tail, and eight pale eyes that radiate a faint sickly luminescence, its signature the petrifying gaze that turns warm flesh to grey stone.

A kelpie rising from the dark loch — a sleek black horse of supernatural sheen, coat smooth as wet obsidian, hooves inverting like those of a deep-water thing, mane flowing with actual water and trailing river-weed, its signature the irresistible glamour that lures riders to their drowning.

A basilisk coiled on shattered stone — a massive eight-legged reptile with iron-dark scales ridged like armour plating, a thick crested skull and lidded yellow eyes that carry a pale corona of deadly light, every surface around it bleached to pale grey stone.

A chimera roaring on a scorched hillside — the great maned head of a lion at its fore, a living goat head sprouting from the middle of its spine, and a coiling viper head topping its serpentine tail, three throats capable of three entirely different forms of death.

A hulking minotaur at the labyrinth threshold — the enormous horned bull head set on a massively muscled human torso, hide the deep reddish-brown of old blood, broad flat nostrils steaming, hooves of black iron, a double-headed axe worn smooth by centuries of use.

A mountain giant looming above the treeline — forty feet of granite-grey skin stretched over boulder-dense muscle, a craggy face eroded like a cliff face by wind and age, knuckles calloused to stone hardness, each footfall leaving craters in the valley floor.

A sphinx crouched on the desert plateau — the serene yet merciless face of a woman set upon the great tawny body of a lion, vast feathered wings folded against her flanks like a pharaoh's cloak, her gaze patient and absolutely unblinking in the burning sun.

A manticore stalking the red barrens — a lion's powerfully muscled tawny body bearing a grotesque human-like face of iron teeth, leathery bat wings spanning wide overhead, and a long scorpion tail arching forward, its cluster of venomous spines capable of launching like thrown javelins.

A cyclops on the sea-cliff — a man-shaped giant of pale scarred hide, fifteen feet of corded muscle and enormous appetite, and at the centre of its low broad forehead a single vast eye the amber-gold colour of firelight, eerily beautiful and utterly unblinking.

Cerberus guarding the underworld gate — three massive mastiff heads on a single enormous canine body, each neck ringed with a mane of coiling serpents, obsidian-black fur bristling, six eyes glowing ember-red, the ground charred black beneath paws the size of millstones.

A colossal sea-serpent breaching the ocean — a leviathan of smooth blue-black scales each the size of a shield, a neck like a cathedral column erupting from churning white water, a head of crushing jaw and cold pale eye, its submerged body spanning the length of a warship.

A winged pegasus against a storm sky — a great white stallion of powerful arched neck and deep chest, its coat like polished moonstone, but erupting from the shoulders a magnificent pair of feathered wings spanning thirty feet, each primary feather edged with a faint silver luminescence.

A frost giant striding across a glacier — a colossus of blue-white skin latticed with cracks like glacial ice, lank white hair crusted with rime, exhaling blizzard-cold breath with every step, wielding a club of ancient glacier-ice dense and green at its core and never melting.

A kelpie emerging from the black loch — the sleek form of a magnificent dark horse with water-weed threaded through its mane and hide glistening like wet slate, but its hooves reversed, its eyes holding the flat cold light of deep water, standing preternaturally still at the shore.

A great owlbear deep in the midnight forest — the barrel-chested body of a grizzly bear covered in dense tawny-brown feathers that bristle along the spine, a broad flat owl face of pale facial disc and enormous amber eyes, taloned forepaws capable of both rending and silent arboreal climbing.

A wendigo howling across the frozen barrens — a gaunt towering figure of exposed bone and taut grey skin, antler tines erupting from its skull, enormous hollow eye sockets lit with a cold blue hunger-light, exhaling visible cold, its elongated limbs moving with impossible loping swiftness across deep snow.

A stone gargoyle come to grotesque life — a hunched winged figure whose entire body is living grey granite, surface pitted and weathered, bat-like wings of cracked stone spreading stiffly, a carved grimace become a true snarl, and eyes that shift from dark stone to burning sulphur-yellow.

A hippogriff banking on a mountain thermal — the proud eagle head, razor talons and great feathered wings of a raptor joined seamlessly to the dappled hindquarters and flashing hooves of a horse, feather-to-hide transition a marvel of interlocked quills, amber eyes fierce as any hawk's.

A roc blotting the midday sun — a raptor of catastrophic scale, each wing spanning the width of a river, talons curved like war-galleys, the beak a battering ram of pale horn, the down-draft of a single wingbeat flattening forest canopy and rolling ships onto their sides below.

A cockatrice stalking the courtyard — the body of a scaled rooster on two clawed legs, leathery two-winged bat-like wings half-spread for balance, a serpentine barbed tail, and the single most dangerous feature being its small beady eyes ringed with pale gold fire that calcify living flesh on contact.

A banshee drifting above the ruined keep — a translucent female figure of cold silver-white luminescence, long hair streaming in a wind that exists only for her, hollow black eye sockets pooling shadow, her mouth opening in a keening wail that is less heard than felt as ice forming along the spine.

A colossal kraken heaving from black water — mountainous mottled-purple flesh, eight barnacled tentacles each thicker than a ship's mast lined with pale suckers, two vast feeding arms coiling overhead, a single baleful eye the diameter of a cartwheel regarding the surface with ancient malice.

A many-headed hydra coiled in the marsh shallows — a serpentine body the length of a war galley, scales of deep olive-green edged in black, nine long necks rearing each topped with a flat fanged skull, each head independently tracking prey, yellow slit-pupils glittering with cold hunger.

A monstrous troll crouching on the riverbank — a hulking asymmetrical body of grey-green warty hide, massive sloping shoulders, arms hanging past knobbed knees, a flat broad-nostriled face with small red eyes beneath a ridged brow, long clawed fingers trailing in the current, its ONE terrible feature the wound closing before your eyes.

A basilisk on its rocky promontory — a low-slung reptile body the size of a bull, eight clawed legs splayed wide, scales of dusty iron-grey edged in yellow, a crested skull carrying eight small eyes, the front two burning a pale sulfurous gold that turns living flesh to veined grey stone wherever that gaze falls.

A chimera rearing on a scorched hillside — the maned lion forepart, tawny and scarred, merged with a shaggy goat midsection bearing a second head on its spine, the horned goat face braying with two sets of teeth, a long serpent tail rearing a hissing viper skull at its tip, three throats breathing smoke.

A hulking minotaur standing in the labyrinth threshold — a barrel-chested human body seven feet tall sheathed in coarse dark fur at the haunches, a massive bull's head with wide ebony horns, a wet black muzzle, broad nostrils flared and steaming, heavy hooves striking sparks from the stone floor.

A mountain giant standing knee-deep in the pass — forty feet of coarse-skinned flesh the color of granite, a great craggy face half-buried in a tangled grey beard, enormous fists wrapped around a pine trunk used as a staff, boulders hanging at its belt like pebbles, each footfall shaking loose stones from the cliff face.

A sphinx at rest on the desert plinth — a human face of severe beauty, eyes of polished malachite set in tawny fur, great eagle wings folded in bands of cream and russet against a lion's powerful body, tail curled around stone paws, its ONE devastating feature the riddle whose wrong answer means instant annihilation.

A manticore poised on the cliff edge — a lion's heavily muscled tawny body, a broad human face with three rows of inward-curving teeth, large leathery wings fanned for balance, and a scorpion tail arched high overhead, each hollow spine loaded with a venomous quill it can launch with a flick like a crossbow bolt.

A cyclops braced in the cave entrance — a towering humanoid form, twelve feet of dense ropy muscle under rough olive skin, a single enormous eye dominating the broad flat face, small curved horns above the brow, a club of whole pine tree dangling in one fist, the eye blinking slowly with all the indifferent calm of a lighthouse beam.

Cerberus standing at the obsidian gate — one massive hound body the size of a draft horse, black short fur over bunched musculature, three wolf-skulled heads on thick necks each bristling with a separate mane, six amber eyes burning with heatsink-orange fire, a serpent for a tail striking the air, each head growling a different pitch simultaneously.

A colossal sea-serpent breaching the grey ocean — a neck fifty feet of scale-plated olive-black rising from the chop, a long blunt crocodilian skull, ridged back fins like sails slicing the surface, the vast body coiled beneath glimpsed as shadow darker than the deep, displacement waves rolling outward like the sea itself is breathing.

A winged pegasus on the mountain crag — a pure-white stallion's body of layered muscle and gleaming coat, enormous swan-white feathered wings spread against the sky, each primary feather edged in silver, hooves shod in natural platinum-pale horn, mane streaming in the high wind, dark liquid eyes carrying the calm awareness of something that knows the shape of clouds from above.

A frost giant striding through the blizzard — a being eighteen feet tall wrapped in fur and blue-white skin glazed with permafrost, a broad face with ice-pale eyes and a beard of frozen braids, each exhaled breath a small storm, wielding a glacier-carved greataxe, runes of cold fire burning along its forearms.

A kelpie at the loch's edge at dusk — appearing first as a sleek grey horse with dripping mane, seaweed tangled through its tail, hooves too broad and wet-dark for dry land, nostrils trailing river-mist, the ONE horrifying feature the glistening adhesive hide to which any rider's hands bind fast the moment they touch it.

A great owlbear in the old-growth dark — a bear's massive frame covered in dense brown fur, the head entirely that of a giant horned owl, flat facial disc of pale feathers framing two enormous amber-iris eyes, a sharp curved beak the length of a forearm, feathered ear tufts raised in threat, standing eight feet at the shoulder.

A wendigo in the frozen treeline — a gaunt towering figure of exposed sinew and pale blue skin stretched tight over elongated bone, a rack of jagged antlers rising from a skeletal head, hollow black eye sockets burning with pale cold hunger-fire, long fingers ending in bone-white claws, its passage marked by frost and the smell of deep winter.

A stone gargoyle come alive on the cathedral parapet — a hunched figure of grey animated granite, bat-wings unfolding with a crack of freed stone, clawed hands gripping the cornice, a carved snarling face now genuinely leering, eyes igniting to dull orange, skin still bearing the chisel marks of the mason who thought he was making decoration.

A hippogriff banking in the mountain thermals — the eagle head and feathered forequarters, talons and wings identical to a golden eagle scaled enormous, joined seamlessly to the hindquarters and haunches of a fine bay horse, tail streaming, the feather-to-fur transition a band of cream and chestnut, riding the updraft with the casual mastery of a born aerial predator.

A roc descending from the stratosphere — a raptor body the scale of a sailing vessel, each primary feather the size of a boat's oar, dark-brown plumage edged in gold, a hooked yellow beak large enough to swallow a horse, talons that cast individual shadows the size of houses on the ground below as it stoops.

A cockatrice in the ruined courtyard — a rooster's feathered head and crowing neck on a small dragon's scaled body, leathery wings half-raised, a serpent for a tail flicking the dust, bright spurred legs, a comb of deep red, the ONE lethal feature the crowing gaze that crystallizes warm flesh to grey stone in three heartbeats.

A banshee drifting at the forest's edge — a female figure of cold translucent light, robes of grey mist trailing and dispersing at the hem, hair loose and streaming as though underwater, face a mask of absolute grief, hollow eyes lit from within by pale blue, the ONE unbearable feature the keening wail that builds in the chest before the scream begins.

A many-headed hydra rising from black marsh water — nine serpentine necks of scaled emerald-grey, each crowned with a wedge-shaped fanged head, forked tongues flickering, the bloated crocodilian torso half-submerged, each severed neck already splitting into two regrowths.

A colossal sea-leviathan breaching black water — a whale-scaled body stretching the length of a galleon, plate-sized scales of midnight blue edged with bioluminescent silver, a crocodilian head bearing rows of recurved teeth, fins like cathedral buttresses, the wake of its passage swamping coastlines.

A colossal kraken heaving from the black deep — a mountainous mottled-purple body and vast barnacled tentacles each thicker than a ship's mast, lined with pale suckers rimmed in hooked chitin, one baleful eye the size of a wagon wheel.

A many-headed hydra coiled in black swamp water — nine serpentine necks rising from one vast scaled torso, each wedge-shaped head armored in overlapping emerald scales, jaws dripping pale venom, the severed stumps already splitting into new necks.

A monstrous troll hunched on a granite slab — thick warty hide the grey-green of wet stone, lank black hair hanging in ropes, knuckles dragging the ground, jaws filled with yellowed broken fangs, and a body that visibly knits flesh back over every wound.

A basilisk crouched on shattered flagstones — a massive eight-legged reptile, scales the color of dead moss, broad flat skull crested with a serrated ridge, and two enormous pale eyes radiating a cold amber light that turns living flesh to grey stone.

A chimera rearing on a hilltop — the muscular tawny foreparts and fanged head of a lion, a living goat's head rising on a serpentine neck from mid-spine, a long viper tail hissing at its rear, and a second throat venting a gout of oily flame.

A hulking minotaur in a torchlit labyrinth — seven feet of layered muscle, coal-black fur covering the enormous bull's head with flaring nostrils and curved horns worn to ivory points, human legs planted wide, double-headed axe trailing sparks on stone.

A mountain giant standing against the skyline — forty feet of granite-grey skin over slabbed muscle, hair like grey boulders tumbling, brow ridged and heavy, fists the size of mill wheels, and a voice that rolls like a landslide across the valley below.

A sphinx seated on wind-worn limestone — the broad dignified head and shoulders of a woman above a lion's deep-chested body and great folded wings, tawny fur fading to cream at the chest, eyes gold and ancient, patient as the desert itself.

A manticore prowling the red desert — a lion's tawny body and maned head carrying a grotesquely human face, three rows of serrated teeth packed behind the lips, leathery bat wings folded at the shoulders, a barbed scorpion tail arched forward over its back.

A cyclops striding across a stony plain — twelve feet of pale knotted muscle wrapped in crude hide, one enormous amber eye dominating a low brutish forehead, ragged dark beard, and hands large enough to close around a full-grown ox, dragging an uprooted pine.

A cerberus standing astride the black river — three wolf-like heads on a single massive hound body, each head distinct, scarred fur the color of charcoal, six red eyes burning, serpent heads rising from the spine and tail, a growl that shakes the air.

A colossal sea-serpent breaching a storm-grey ocean — a neck thicker than a longship rising sixty feet from the waves, scales like hammered pewter, a flat crocodilian head ringed with bioluminescent frills, jaw hinged impossibly wide, swallowing the howling sky.

A winged pegasus on a cliff edge — a stallion of pure white, deep-chested and finely muscled, two great swan-feathered wings rising from the withers like living sails, mane streaming in the high wind, hooves striking silver sparks from bare rock.

A frost giant striding through a blizzard — eighteen feet of pale blue-white skin over iron muscle, beard and hair caked in icicles, breath rolling in white clouds, wielding a glacier-hewn club, runes of cold glowing blue-white across the broad scarred chest.

A kelpie rising from a black highland loch — the sleek black-green form of a powerful horse with streaming mane threaded with water-weed and river shells, hooves silent on the water's surface, eyes lit an eerie amber, hide slick and faintly luminous in the mist.

A great owlbear in a moonlit forest — a bear's massive body and heavy claws beneath an enormous disc-faced owl's head, brown-and-tawny feathered ruff blending into dense fur down the shoulders, amber eyes glowing, beak clattering with a sound like cracking bone.

A wendigo against a frozen treeline — impossibly tall and gaunt, grey-blue skin stretched over jutting bone, antlers of blackened dead wood erupting from the skull, breath freezing the air in rags, eyes hollow voids leaking cold pale light, moving without a sound.

A stone gargoyle come alive on a cathedral parapet — squat and powerful, skin the exact grey of carved limestone fissured with old cracks, bat-leather wings unfolding with a grinding scrape, grotesque face split by a toothy grin, claws raking sparks from the stonework.

A hippogriff banking through cloud — the eagle's sharp-hooked beak, golden-feathered head, and massive taloned forelegs fused to the dappled hindquarters and flowing tail of a horse, broad feathered wings beating a thunder of displaced air, keen yellow eyes fixed on prey.

A roc blotting out the sun — a bird of prey scaled to nightmare, each wing spanning a city block, primary feathers the length of longships, talons capable of seizing an elephant, the down-stroke of those wings flattening trees and scattering ships like toys.

A cockatrice strutting across a courtyard — the body of a great scaled rooster with a long barbed serpent tail and small leathery wings, red wattles and a crowing beak, comb crimson as blood, and two golden eyes that calcify whatever living thing they hold.

A banshee drifting across a moonlit moor — a translucent woman-shape in shroud-like rags, long white hair rising in no wind, hands like pale bone, mouth opened in a soundless keening that resonates inside the skull and stops the heart of any who hear it.

A many-headed hydra rising from fetid swamp — nine serpentine necks weaving independently, each crowned with a wedge-shaped skull, ivory fangs dripping venom, scales the deep green of stagnant water, every severed neck sprouting two replacements in gushing torrents of black blood.

A basilisk crouched on shattered stone — a massive eight-legged reptile, scales like tarnished iron, a crest of black spines running from skull to tail, its eight eyes burning with pale amber light, the ground around it littered with grey statues of frozen prey.

A chimera prowling a mountain ridge — the heavy lion's forebody and forelimbs seamlessly joined to a goat's barrel-chested middle, a living serpent for a tail hissing independently, a second goat-horned head rising from its spine, fire guttering between the lion's clenched teeth.

A sphinx couched on desert sandstone — the sleek lioness body of enormous size, paws crossed with patient authority, vast hawk wings folded tight, a serene human face of ageless beauty framed by a golden headdress, eyes holding the luminous calm of accumulated centuries.

A manticore circling its prey — the powerful tawny body of a lion, a grotesque human face set with three rows of serrated teeth, leathery bat wings beating the air, a scorpion tail arched high, its barbs launching volleys of bone-white quills with each flex.

Cerberus guarding the obsidian gate — three snarling wolf-mastiff heads on a single colossal canine body, black fur bristling along a ridge-spine, six eyes burning ember-red, a serpent for a tail, each head operating independently, one sleeping, one sniffing, one baring dripping fangs.

A kelpie rising from a highland loch — appearing first as a sleek black horse of uncanny beauty, mane streaming like water, but the seaweed tangled in its tail and the river-reeds growing from its hide betray the truth, hooves dissolving into rushing current as it surges forward.

A wendigo stalking a frozen forest — a towering emaciated figure of grey skin pulled drum-tight over jutting bone, antlers of black bone erupting from a elongated skull, hollow frost-white eyes, breath reeking in visible plumes, long clawed fingers moving between the pines with inhuman silent speed.

A hippogriff banking on a thermal — the foreparts of an eagle, hooked beak and taloned forelimbs and powerful feathered chest, joined to the hindquarters of a horse, haunches rippling with muscle, a horse's tail streaming, the wings an enormous span of banded brown-and-gold feathers.

A roc descending from the clouds — a bird of such impossible scale that its wingspan blots the sun, feathers each the length of a longboat, talons closing around a full-grown elephant with casual ease, the downwash of its wings flattening a forest below like bent grass.

A cockatrice stalking through underbrush — a rooster's wattled head and scaled neck on the body of a two-legged lizard, small leathery wings half-spread, tail lashing, the signature feature its gaze which turns living flesh to cracked grey stone wherever those yellow eyes fix and hold.

A many-headed hydra rising from a fetid swamp — a vast serpentine body of grey-green scales, slick with marsh water, nine long necks branching like gnarled roots, each crowned with a flat venomous head, fangs dripping acid.

A colossal sea-serpent rising from black water — a body of shimmering blue-black scales each as wide as a shield, a hundred yards of coiling muscle breaking the surface, a flat wedge-shaped head with sail-fin crests, cold yellow eyes.

A kelpie at the river's edge — the sleek form of a black horse, coat perpetually wet and gleaming, mane trailing river-weed, but the hooves reversed and the eyes lamp-yellow, its signature pull: any hand that touches its flank adheres, cannot release.

A stone gargoyle awakened — broad-shouldered and bat-winged, carved granite come to life, cracked lines glowing dull orange at the joints, a grotesque face of horns and fangs grinding open, claws of true stone scraping the parapet, dead eyes now blazing amber fire.

A basilisk crouched on ancient stone — a thick-bodied eight-legged lizard of dull olive scales ridged along the spine, a crested skull and lidded yellow eyes radiating pale cold light, everything within its direct gaze slowly fading to grey marble.

A chimera rearing on massive forelimbs — the great maned lion's head snarling at the fore, a living goat's head rising from the mid-spine bleating with mad eyes, and a scaled serpent's head cresting the tail, three throats breathing three kinds of ruin.

A sphinx seated on a sandstone plinth — the calm imperious head of a woman above a lion's broad-shouldered body, great falcon wings folded with precise elegance, tawny fur blending to smooth bronze skin at the neckline, eyes holding centuries of pitiless knowing.

A manticore on a rocky outcrop — a lion's powerful tawny body and maned head bearing three rows of serrated human-like teeth, a scorpion's armored tail arching overhead bristling with iron-hard spines that it launches with lethal precision across vast distance.

A colossal sea-serpent leviathan breaching — a body of blue-black armored scales hundreds of feet long, a crocodilian head crowned with swept-back horns, finned crests running the spine, water cascading from its flanks in white cataracts as it eclipses the horizon.

A kelpie at a midnight river — a sleek horse of impossible black, coat wet and gleaming like deep water, mane trailing like riverweed, nostrils flaring steam, hooves soundless on the bank, its eyes swirling with a fathomless drowning darkness that compels approach.

A wendigo emerging from the treeline — an emaciated giant of grey-white skin stretched over visible ribs and jutting joints, a rack of antlers rising from the skull, hollow sunken eyes lit with cold blue hunger, every step leaving frost-blackened prints in the soil.

A hippogriff stooping from altitude — the proud crested eagle head and fierce taloned forelegs of a raptor fused seamlessly to the chestnut-and-bay hindquarters and long tail of a horse, barred feather-wings beating in powerful strokes, eyes fixed on prey with predatory precision.

A roc blocking the sun — a bird of incomprehensible scale, feathers each the length of a longship, a curved yellow beak that could engulf a castle tower, talons like anchors, its downbeat generating hurricane winds, shadow alone plunging the land into sudden darkness.

A cockatrice strutting on scaled legs — the wattled rooster head and neck on a compact reptile body of iridescent green-black scales, leathery bat wings half-spread for balance, a barbed serpentine tail lashing, its crowing cry cracking stone, its direct gaze calcifying flesh to dead grey rock.

A banshee wraith keening over the moorland — a translucent female form of blue-white spectral light, long hair streaming in a wind from nowhere, hollow eyes blazing with grief-fire, her mouth open in a silent shriek that nonetheless tears the air and stops hearts cold.

A many-headed hydra rising from fetid marsh — nine serpentine necks each thick as a barrel, scaled in wet emerald and black, each head bearing rows of recurved fangs, every severed stump sprouting two glistening replacements within a heartbeat.
